question: In the pyrolysis of oil shale kerogen, by how many degrees does the maximum of the H2 signal occur earlier under air than under nitrogen?
expect: about 120 C: maximum near 330 C in air vs near 450 C in nitrogen (sec. 3.3.1)
trap: the 50 C earlier onset of mass loss
rendered:
According to page 4, the characteristic H2 signal appears at lower temperatures under air (approximately 250−600 °C, with a maximum near 330 °C) than under nitrogen (approximately 300−800 °C, with a maximum near 450 °C). 

The maximum of the H2 signal occurs 120 °C (450 - 330) earlier under air than under nitrogen.
